🌟 Word of the Day: RESILIENT

📖 Meaning: able to recover quickly after difficulties.
💬 Example: She is so resilient that she bounces back from every setback.

✍️ Your turn! Write your own sentence with "resilient" in the comments 👇

#Speaklo #LearnEnglish #EnglishVocabulary #WordOfTheDay

📘 Grammar Tip: SINCE vs FOR

✅ Use FOR with a period of time: for 3 years, for two hours.
✅ Use SINCE with a starting point: since 2020, since Monday.

💬 Example: I have lived here for 5 years. / I have lived here since 2021.

✍️ Write your own sentence with "since" or "for" in the comments 👇

#Speaklo #LearnEnglish #EnglishGrammar #SinceVsFor

❌✅ Common Mistake

❌ I am agree with you.
✅ I agree with you.

"Agree" is already a verb, so we don't use "am" before it.

📖 Meaning: to start a conversation in an awkward situation.

🌟 Word of the Day: THRIVE

📖 Meaning: to grow and be successful or healthy.
💬 Example: Plants thrive in warm, sunny places.

📘 Grammar Tip: A vs AN

✅ Use A before a consonant SOUND: a book, a university.
✅ Use AN before a vowel SOUND: an apple, an hour.

💡 It's about the sound, not the letter!

✍️ Write your own sentence with "a" or "an" in the comments 👇

#Speaklo #LearnEnglish #EnglishGrammar #AvsAn

❌✅ Common Mistake

❌ We discussed about the plan.
✅ We discussed the plan.

"Discuss" already means "talk about", so we don't add "about".

📘 Grammar Tip: Present Simple vs Present Continuous

✅ Present simple = habits and facts: She works every day.
✅ Present continuous = happening now: She is working now.

✍️ Write one sentence for each in the comments 👇

#Speaklo #LearnEnglish #EnglishGrammar #PresentTense

❌✅ Common Mistake

❌ I look forward to see you.
✅ I look forward to seeing you.

Here "to" is a preposition, so the verb after it takes -ing.

📘 Grammar Tip: MUCH vs MANY

✅ MANY goes with countable nouns: many books, many friends.
✅ MUCH goes with uncountable nouns: much water, much time.

💡 We use them mostly in questions and negatives:
"How many books do you have?" / "I don't have much time."

✍️ Write your own sentence with "much" or "many" in the comments 👇

#Speaklo #LearnEnglish #EnglishGrammar #MuchVsMany
items.source: Cambridge Grammar: much + uncountable, many + plural countable; mostly questions/negatives
